messages:
maya: heads-up — ran a quick perf sweep on qwen2.5 with the new rope-scaling patch. seeing weird throughput cliffs at seq_len ~384 when using the kernel-selector v3 

kevin: can you paste the profiling snippet? is it kernel handoff or batching drop? :thinking_face: 

maya: pasted below. TL;DR: kernel_selector picked the fused-attn kernel until 360, then switched to generic attention and latency jumped +18%. KV cache hit rates steady.

maya: ```
# perf sample
seq_len=320: avg_token_ms=1.8 (fused-attn)
seq_len=384: avg_token_ms=2.1 (generic-attn)
seq_len=512: avg_token_ms=2.15 (generic-attn)
batch=8, model=qwen2.5, heads=32, kv_heads=16
```

alok: that head/kv mismatch screams kernel-compat fallback. kernel_selector likely enforces kv_head==heads or chooses conservative path when packing fails. did you try forcing kernel v2?

maya: forced to kernel v2 (older heuristic) and got consistent fused-attn up to 512, but throughput slightly worse at small seqs. so v3 is better overall but the cutoff is hurting some mid-length workloads.

iris: tokenizer note — we also have a multi-lang input that produces token-splits with lots of non-ascii. could be changing alignment and triggering different kernel codepath because of memory layout? strange but plausible.

kevin: do we have the kernel_selector decision log for that run? there is an option KERNEL_DEBUG=1 to dump reason codes.

maya: grabbed logs. decision reason: "rope_scale_mismatch" at 384 for layer 10, fallback to generic.

alok: rope_scale_mismatch — hmm. that means our RoPE scaling table interpolator detected an out-of-range position frequency and rejected the fused path. what are the rope params? qwen2.5 uses 1500 base?

maya: model config: rope_base=10000, scale_mode=interpolate-linear, head_dim=64, kv_head_dim=64. But we saw an off-by-one in tokenizer output length due to multibyte chars. some inputs add an extra BOS-like token when we normalize.

iris: that would shift absolute positions and could make interpolation hit an edge case. we should make the interpolator tolerant +/-1 and add unit test for multibyte token boundary.

kevin: suggested quick mitigation: alter kernel_selector to prefer fused-attn if fallback reason is solely rope_scale_mismatch and head/kv dims are equal. keep a flag SKIP_ROPE_STRICT_CHECK=true for canary.

maya: tried SKIP_ROPE_STRICT_CHECK=true in a canary, results: avg_token_ms at 384 down to 1.82, and no correctness regressions on 100 eval prompts.

alok: great. can we add a batching heuristic too? the observed cliff also correlates with batching boundary (batch*seq crosses 3072 tokens). sometimes the runtime switches tiling strategy.

maya: yes, batching profile showed that at batch=12 seq=256 (total 3072) we flipped tiling and lost some warps. adding soft-bounds to prefer fewer batches avoided that.

iris: notes to include in PR: 1) relax rope interpolator tolerance, 2) add tokenizer normalization test (multibyte), 3) flag to skip strict rope check for canary, 4) kernel_selector telemetry to emit reason code with layer/context, 5) batching soft-bound heuristic to avoid tiling flip on mid-range tokens.

kevin: also add a unit test for head/kv mismatch: explicitly test heads != kv_heads path to ensure we fallback intentionally and document perf hit.

maya: filing the CL now. also cc @runtime-ci — please run nightly perf regression across qwen2, qwen2.5, and mixtral with both ALiBi and RoPE variants. include multilingual tokenizer seeds.

runtime-ci: job queued: 1769001301. will run qwen2/qwen2.5/mixtral matrix, include tokenization fuzz seeds (zh, ja, ru, de), report back with kernel reason distribution and avg token ms.

kevin: one more thought — we saw head_dim==kv_head_dim in this run but the model zoos have some models with grouped-kv where dims differ. ensure selector checks grouping not equality.

maya: noted. updating the selector logic to check grouping compatibility instead of strict equality. will draft PR and link perf numbers in the thread. :thumbsup:
